A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same capacity-aware MoE inference research, with matching titles, authors, and substantial shared material. Text and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, results, and complete appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-benchmark evaluations, inference speedups, expert-load measurements, and capacity and rerouting ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original language and multimodal evaluations, latency breakdowns, expert-load measurements, and routing ablations, including results in Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: v1's Token Reroute repeatedly masks overloaded assignments and reselects experts. v2 replaces this with Expanded Drop: combine top-k selections with local expert candidates, then enforce capacity limits, allowing tokens to retain more than k experts. Section 5.3 also introduces modality-prioritized dropping. These change the inference procedure beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The nine language benchmarks are retained. v2 adds vision-language evaluation using MolmoE on MME, MMBench, and SEED-Bench, covering visual perception and multimodal reasoning absent from v1 (Section 5.3 and Appendix B).

E2.justification: The dropless baseline, Expert Drop, and Order/Reverse Order/Random/Score comparisons remain. v2 additionally evaluates global expansion against local Expanded Drop in Figure 6, and compares Uniform, Text First, and Image First policies in Table 3.

E3.justification: Reported timing hardware changes from A30 to H20 GPUs. New protocols include component-level timing, multimodal scoring at capacity factors 0.5–1.5, and maximum-k controls in Table 7. Language-task shot counts and metrics remain unchanged (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). v2 Figure 4's six-GPU Qwen annotation conflicts with its general eight-GPU description.

E4.justification: v1's rerouting-round ablation is removed. v2 adds global-versus-local latency decomposition, load redistribution, modality-priority comparisons, token-composition analysis, and an ablation of enforcing at most k experts per token (Figure 6, Figures 8–9, Tables 3 and 7). The original layer-wise load and dropped-token analyses remain in renumbered Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report averages over multiple random seeds without specifying their number. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting practice. Changed averages do not establish changed statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 removes the capacity-3.0 block and revises scores, including OLMoE Score at capacity 1.0 averaging 57.8 versus 61.1. Latency results are replaced: v1 reports a 1.37× Mixtral end-to-end speedup, while v2 reports 1.85× for Expanded Drop under changed hardware and procedures. Multimodal and new ablation results are added. Table 2's numerical values remain identical, but Token Reroute rows are now attributed to Expanded Drop.

T1.justification: The expert-load and capacity definitions, maximum-load latency bounds, and dropped-token formula are retained. Filtering equations are recast using retained high-score assignments rather than rejected low-score assignments. No new theoretical result, formal assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central straggler-effect and Token Drop claims remain, but the second methodological contribution becomes local Expanded Drop rather than iterative Token Reroute. The abstract and introduction expand the claimed applicability to multimodal MoE and claim that aggressive capacity constraints can preserve performance by exploiting image-token redundancy.

C2.justification: v1 describes rerouting overhead as minimal; v2 characterizes repeated reselection as costly and motivates local expansion through communication overhead. v2 adds explanations based on image-token redundancy and unrestricted expert selection, and changes the recommended performance-preserving capacity from 2.0 to 1.5. v1's explicit limitations concerning architecture coverage and untested training integration are removed.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C supplies tensor-level pseudocode for Token Drop and Expanded Drop, including local expert IDs, concatenation, scatter operations, and capacity masks, replacing v1's higher-level rerouting pseudocode. Local processing before All-to-All communication is explained, and hardware information is revised. The existing LM-Harness evaluation details remain, without a newly provided implementation release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Molmo, MME, MMBench, SEED-Bench, and image-token redundancy, while removing Lo et al.'s discussion of MoE initialization and imbalance. The main positioning against training-time balancing and redundant expert deployment remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The principal section sequence and much shared exposition remain. Revisions concentrate on the abstract, introductory motivation, and low-load method explanation; a multimodal subsection is inserted, pseudocode is placed in an expanded appendix, and the Limitations section is removed. This is localized narrative restructuring rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 3 is redrawn as a device-routing diagram; latency displays are rebuilt and separated; profiling, load-distribution, and multimodal figures and tables are added. The rerouting-round figure disappears, while the original appendix plots are retained with new placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more useful evidence for its implementation choices through the communication breakdown in Figure 6, maximum-k ablation in Appendix D, and modality-priority controls, alongside more explicit pseudocode. These improve assessability. The gain is tempered by unexplained identical Table 2 scores under the revised method attribution and removal of explicit limitations. Broad low-capacity performance-preservation claims also need qualification: SEED-Bench Expanded Drop at capacity 0.5 scores 65.5 overall versus the 68.7 baseline (Table 6).
